item.title: HSC pass rate hits 22-year low, over 5 lakh fail

item.title: Student unions at five universities hog headlines for wrong reasons

item.title: A digital trail to track learning gaps
item.description: The government is planning a digital platform to store assessment records of students from classes 1 to 12, helping teachers track their progress and identify learning gaps.

item.title: Schools up, pupils down
item.description: Bangladesh has more secondary schools than it did seven years ago, but far fewer students in them.

item.title: Who protects families when they report child sexual abuse?

item.title: Bewildering convictions
item.description: The jailing of 85 people following a raid on a senior police officer’s house in Purbachal last week has raised questions over the evidence behind their convictions and the circulation of their photographs and videos.

item.title: Govt plans Tk 21,900cr digital makeover for schools
item.description: According to proposals by the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education (DSHE), the projects will cover half of the 20,767 secondary and higher secondary educational institutions and be implemented between January 2027 and December 2031.

item.title: The PM must be protected. But who protects the ordinary citizen?

item.title: Give SSC students who failed a second chance, but fix the learning gaps too
item.description: Last week, Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon announced that SSC examinees who failed two subjects could retake those exams within 15 days of the results.

item.title: Durga Puja: The joy of coming home
item.description: Sharadiya Durga Puja is here again. Across Dhaka, temples and puja mandaps are dressed in festive colours, ready to welcome devotees. Families gather, friends reunite, and children accompany their parents to see the goddess. Devotees bow before the idols, offer anjali and receive prasad.

item.title: Why must the girl change her route?
item.description: From harassment and threats to retaliation against families who speak up, the burden of safety continues to fall on girls while perpetrators often face little immediate consequence

item.title: Secondary schools: Vacant posts hurting children, taxing teachers
item.description: Persistent shortages of teachers have been disrupting classroom learning at secondary schools across the country, forcing many institutions to overburden teachers of key subjects including mathematics, English and ICT, and reduce the frequency of practical classes.

item.title: School textbooks to get new content on history
item.description: School textbooks will be revised for the 2027 academic year, with new content on the Liberation War, post-independence political history and the July Uprising.

item.description: Seven years after Abrar Fahad’s killing, I revisit what I wrote that day about campus violence, political labels and the silence that allowed it to continue.

item.title: Can BNP protect journalists from its own rank and file?

item.title: I get Eid off. Do my journalist colleagues get the same for Puja?

item.title: Manush, tumi emon keno?
item.description: We can stop for a bird, hold an umbrella over a stranger and enter a river to save a life. We can also humiliate, hurt and kill. The distance between those two versions of us is sometimes painfully small.

item.title: Dear fellow journalists; We report everyone else's fight for fair pay. What about our wage board?
item.description: For many journalists, the last wage structure that reached their newsroom dates to 2013. With the Ninth still largely unimplemented, the harder question is whether any new award would actually be enforced.

item.title: We are sorry, Tofazzel
item.description:
For a few minutes, Tofazzel was sitting in a canteen eating rice like anyone else. Someone had to serve him the food. Someone watched him eat. Someone spoke to him. Then he was taken back and beaten again.
How does a person do both?
